idiom_name: contextvars.ContextVar / Context (PEP 567); framework-scoped g and request objects
implementation_notes: Python's standard library provides the ambient carrier: a ContextVar is declared at module level, set once per request with set() (keeping the Token for reset) and read in any function called from that task, because every asyncio task and every thread runs inside its own Context that copy_context() can snapshot explicitly. Web frameworks layer their own request-scoped object on top - Flask's g and request proxies, Django's request, or a request-scoped DI container - which is the right choice when the value only travels inside one handler; the hand-written context-plus-factory class remains justified in libraries that must not depend on the framework, where the context is passed explicitly instead.
code_sketch:
import contextvars
request_ctx: contextvars.ContextVar["RequestContext"] = contextvars.ContextVar("request_ctx")

async def handle(request):
    token = request_ctx.set(RequestContext(request))   # Context Factory
    try:
        await dispatch()                               # no context argument below
    finally:
        request_ctx.reset(token)                       # bounded lifetime

def tenant_id() -> int:
    return request_ctx.get().tenant_id
pitfalls: A ContextVar created inside a function is recreated on every call and, once referenced by a long-lived Context, is never garbage-collected - the docs require declaring it at module level.
Values flow into tasks as a snapshot taken when the task is created: a set() performed afterwards is invisible to that task, and threads never share contextvars with the thread that created them.
